preferred_method.label: Balance method — do the same to both sides

materials.heading: Common mistake: why the sign changes
materials.excerpt:
Some pupils write 7x = 15 because they move the 2x across the equals sign without changing it — a sign error when moving a term.
We never 'move' a term: we do the same to both sides to keep it balanced, so the 2x is subtracted from both sides.

materials.heading: Practice: unknowns on both sides
materials.excerpt: Solve 7x − 2 = 3x + 10 and 4x + 5 = x − 7. Check each answer by substituting back — both sides should have the same value.
materials.why: aligned to Solve linear equations with the unknown on both sides; uses Balance method — do the same to both sides

materials.heading: Worked example: x on both sides
materials.excerpt:
Solve 5x + 3 = 2x + 12. Draw the bar model for each side of the balance.
Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x + 3 = 12. Subtract 3 from both sides: 3x = 9, so x = 3.
